name_en: Kobu Zushi — sushi rice rolled in kelp alone, no filling at its core
summary_ja: 芯に具を入れず酢飯を昆布で巻くすしで、県中央部は白い板昆布を使う「板こぶずし」、県西部は黒い昆布を甘辛く煮た「黒こぶずし」に分かれる。冠婚葬祭で客に持たせる折箱にも入るという。
summary_en: Vinegared rice is rolled in kelp alone, with nothing at the core — central Kochi uses thin white sheet kelp for itakobu-zushi, while the west uses kelp simmered sweet and salty for kurokobu-zushi. It's also packed into the boxed take-home gifts given to guests at celebrations.
source_title: こぶずし 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Ginburo Zushi — sushi rice mixed with a rare local bean grown by only a few families
summary_ja: 大豊町西豊永地区で自家用に栽培されてきたいんげん豆「銀ぶろう」を甘く煮て、根菜とともに酢飯に混ぜ込むすし。不老長寿の豆として縁起物とされ、祝宴や祭事のときにつくられてきたという。
summary_en: Ginburo, a kidney bean grown only for home use in a district of Otoyo Town, is simmered sweet and folded into vinegared rice with root vegetables. Regarded as a bean of long life and good fortune, it's traditionally made for festivals and celebratory banquets.
source_title: 銀ぶろうずし 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Saba no Sugata Zushi — a whole mackerel, cured and packed with sushi rice, head and tail intact
summary_ja: サバを背開きにして塩と酢でしめ、腹に酢飯をぎっしり詰めて頭と尾を立てて仕上げる皿鉢料理の定番。京都のさばずしより酢と塩を効かせた味付けとされ、脂の少ないゴマサバの持ち味に合わせているという。
summary_en: Mackerel is butterflied, cured in salt and vinegar, and packed tight with sushi rice, finished with the head and tail set upright — a fixture of sawachi platters. Its seasoning leans harder on vinegar and salt than Kyoto's saba-zushi, said to suit the leaner blue mackerel more commonly caught off Kochi.
source_title: さばの姿ずし 高知県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
